initial_requirements: A university needs a Unified University Inventory System that combines the inventory databases of three faculties and makes the integrated inventory available through a secure web interface. University, faculty, and department staff need to manage assets such as rooms, software licences, and equipment, while other users should be able to request assets or reserve spaces for approval by the appropriate administrative level.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary outcomes or success criteria you want this Unified University Inventory System to achieve for the university, such as improvements in visibility, control, approval processing, or consolidation of the three faculty inventories?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main outcome is to have one reliable source of truth for all three faculties instead of separate inventory records that don’t always match. We want staff to be able to see what assets exist, where they are, and who is responsible for them, with much better control over approvals for requests and reservations. Another big success factor is reducing duplicate data entry and manual coordination, so requests move faster and the university can manage rooms, licences, and equipment in a more consistent way.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which specific user groups and approval roles should the system support (for example university-level administrators, faculty and department staff, asset custodians, and requesters), and what permissions or responsibilities should each role have?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We’d need university-level administrators, faculty administrators, department staff, asset custodians or inventory managers, and general requesters. The university-level people should have oversight across all faculties and be able to approve or override things that affect the whole institution, while faculty and department staff handle approvals within their own scope. Custodians should maintain the asset records and update availability, and requesters should only be able to search, submit requests, and make reservations for approval.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you describe the approval workflow for asset requests and space reservations in detail, including the approval steps, who can approve at each level, how escalation or overrides should work, and any differences in workflow for university-wide versus faculty- or department-level requests?
turns.interviewee_utterance: For department-level items, I’d expect the request to start with the requester, then go to the department staff or custodian who owns that asset or space, and then to the faculty level if the request has a bigger impact or exceeds local authority. For university-wide assets or higher-risk reservations, it should escalate to the university administrator after the faculty review, and only the appropriate level should be able to approve at each step. Overrides should be possible for senior administrators in exceptional cases, but those should be logged clearly so we can audit why the normal path was bypassed.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What notifications should the system send for inventory requests, reservations, approvals, rejections, escalations, and overrides, and who should receive them in each case?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Users should get notifications when they submit a request or reservation, when it’s approved, rejected, escalated, or overridden, and also when a reservation is nearing its start or end date. The requester should always be notified, and the next approver in the chain should be alerted immediately when action is needed. For overrides or escalations, I’d also want the relevant department or faculty staff to be informed, so nothing is changed without the right people knowing.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When users search the unified inventory and when the three faculty databases are migrated into the new system, what search and filter capabilities are needed, and what data cleansing, deduplication, mapping, or validation rules should be applied during migration to ensure the combined inventory is accurate and consistent?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Search should let users find assets by things like name, type, location, faculty, department, status, and availability, and it would help if they can also filter by booking dates for rooms or by licence expiry for software. During migration, we’d need to clean up duplicate records, standardize field names and codes across the three faculties, and validate anything missing or conflicting before it goes live. If the same asset appears in more than one database, we’d need a clear rule for matching and merging it, but I’d need to check with the faculty teams for the exact matching criteria.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When the same asset appears in more than one faculty database, what rules should we use to identify matches and decide which record becomes the master record, including how to handle conflicts in ownership, location, or other key fields?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We should treat records as a match if they have the same asset tag or serial number, and if those are missing then we’d use a combination of name, model, and location to compare them. The master record should be the most complete and most recently verified one, ideally from the faculty that actually owns the asset, but if ownership conflicts we’d need a human review rather than forcing an automatic merge. For conflicting fields like location or custodian, I’d prefer we keep the approved current value and store the other values in an audit trail so nothing is lost.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Create one reliable source of truth for inventory across all three faculties; improve visibility of what assets exist, where they are, and who is responsible for them; strengthen control over approval of requests and reservations; reduce duplicate data entry and manual coordination; speed up request processing; manage rooms, software licences, and equipment more consistently.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: University-level administrators with oversight across all faculties and authority to approve or override institution-wide matters; faculty administrators and department staff who approve requests within their own scope; asset custodians or inventory managers who maintain asset records and update availability; general requesters who can search assets, submit requests, and make reservations.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Support searching inventory, submitting asset requests, and making space reservations; allow asset custodians to maintain asset records and update availability; route requests and reservations through the appropriate approval levels; support approvals and overrides by authorized staff; provide a secure web interface for users to access the integrated inventory; send notifications on submission, approval, rejection, escalation, override, and upcoming reservation start/end dates; allow searching by asset name, type, location, faculty, department, status, availability, booking dates for rooms, and licence expiry for software.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Only the appropriate approval level may approve a request at each step; department-level items start with the requester and go to the owning department staff or custodian, then escalate to faculty level if needed; university-wide assets or higher-risk reservations escalate to university administration after faculty review; senior administrators may override the normal approval path in exceptional cases, and overrides must be clearly logged for audit purposes; the requester must always be notified, and the next approver in the chain must be alerted immediately when action is needed.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Assets including rooms, software licences, and equipment; inventory records for the three faculties; responsibility/ownership records identifying who is responsible for each asset; request records; reservation records; approval records; override/audit log entries; notification records/messages.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: The system must combine inventory databases from three faculties; access must be through a secure web interface; approval authority must respect organizational scope and hierarchy; some approvals may need escalation based on impact or risk; overrides require audit logging; notifications must be triggered for relevant request and reservation events.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: High data consistency and reliability across faculty inventories; improved visibility of asset location and responsibility; faster processing of requests and reservations; reduced duplicate data entry and manual coordination; clear traceability for approvals and overrides; timely delivery of notifications for workflow events and reservation reminders.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: If a request exceeds local authority or has broader impact, it must escalate to the next approval level; if a reservation is high-risk or university-wide, it must proceed to university administration after faculty review; exceptional overrides by senior administrators are allowed but must be recorded; notifications should still be sent when items are approved, rejected, escalated, overridden, or approaching reservation start/end dates.

slots.name: functional_scope
slots.value: Unified inventory management for three faculties; web-based search and viewing of integrated inventory; management of rooms, software licences, and equipment; request and reservation submission; multi-level approval workflow; asset record maintenance and availability updates; override logging; notification delivery for workflow and reservation events.

slots.name: approval_workflow_rules
slots.value: Requests originate with the requester and are routed first to the owner of the asset or space at the department level, then to faculty review if the request exceeds local authority, and finally to university administration for university-wide or high-risk cases; only the designated level may approve at each stage; senior administrators may override in exceptional cases; requester notifications are required at submission and on workflow outcome, and the next approver must be notified when action is needed.

slots.name: asset_classification_model
slots.value: The inventory includes rooms, software licences, and equipment as managed asset types; assets are associated with their location and responsible organizational unit or custodian.

slots.name: integration_requirements
slots.value: Integrate the inventory databases of three faculties into one unified system and make the combined inventory available through a secure web interface.

slots.name: audit_and_history_requirements
slots.value: Override actions must be logged clearly so auditors can see why the normal approval path was bypassed.

slots.name: notification_requirements
slots.value: Notify users when they submit a request or reservation, when it is approved, rejected, escalated, or overridden, and when a reservation is nearing its start or end date; the requester must always be notified, the next approver must be alerted immediately, and relevant department or faculty staff should also be informed for escalations or overrides.

slots.name: search_and_filter_requirements
slots.value: Users should be able to search assets by name, type, location, faculty, department, status, and availability, and filter by booking dates for rooms or by software licence expiry.

slots.name: data_migration_and_cleaning_requirements
slots.value: During migration, duplicate records should be cleaned up, field names and codes should be standardized across the three faculties, and missing or conflicting data should be validated before go-live; if the same asset appears in more than one database, a matching and merging rule is needed, though the exact criteria are still to be confirmed with the faculty teams.

slots.name: authentication_and_access_control_requirements
slots.value: The system should provide secure web access with role-based permissions so that university administrators, faculty administrators, department staff, custodians, and requesters can only perform the actions allowed by their role and organizational scope.

slots.name: reporting_and_audit_view_requirements
slots.value: The system should provide audit and history views that let authorized users review approval decisions, overrides, and changes made during migration or normal operation, including why normal approval paths were bypassed.

slots.name: asset_deduplication_and_matching_rules
slots.value: Treat records as a match if they have the same asset tag or serial number; if those identifiers are missing, compare a combination of name, model, and location; use the most complete and most recently verified record as the master where ownership is clear.

slots.name: master_record_ownership_governance
slots.value: The master record should ideally come from the faculty that owns the asset; if ownership conflicts, a human review is required rather than automatic merging.

slots.name: conflict_resolution_during_migration
slots.value: If there are conflicts in ownership, do not force an automatic merge; require human review. For conflicting fields such as location or custodian, keep the approved current value and preserve the alternative values in an audit trail.

slots.name: data_quality_validation_criteria
slots.value: Before go-live, validate missing or conflicting data, standardize field names and codes across faculties, and ensure duplicate records are cleaned up and merged according to the agreed matching rules.

slots.name: migration_go_live_cutover_strategy
slots.value: Validate and clean data before go-live, including duplicate cleanup, standardization, and conflict checking; the exact cutover approach is not yet specified.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The user explicitly highlighted that the same asset may appear in more than one faculty database and that matching/merging criteria are still undecided, which suggests the migration phase may have unresolved master-data conflicts and identity resolution challenges.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This likely indicates the three faculties have been maintaining overlapping inventory records independently for some time, so the integrated system will need a deliberate master-data governance approach to prevent duplicate assets, ownership disputes, and incorrect approval routing after consolidation.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The stakeholder emphasized that ownership conflicts during migration must trigger human review rather than automatic merging, and that conflicting values should be preserved in an audit trail instead of overwritten.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This suggests the university expects governance-sensitive records where asset ownership and custodianship may be disputed across faculties, so the system needs controlled exception handling to prevent incorrect consolidation, preserve accountability, and support later audits or dispute resolution.
